item.title: uSync 19.0.0-beta01
item.description:
This is the first beta of uSync for Umbraco v19. It's built against Umbraco 19.0.0-beta1 on .NET 11.
> [!WARNING] > This is a beta for testing against the Umbraco 19 betas. Don't run it on a production site.
## Changes
### uSync has its own Synchronisation section
uSync now opens in its own **Synchronisation** section instead of the Settings tree.
![The uSync dashboard in the Synchronisation section](https://github.com/KevinJump/uSync/releases/download/v19.0.0-beta01/usync19-section.png)
- On first boot, uSync gives the new section to the **Administrators** group. Other groups don't get it automatically, so add it to any group that needs uSync (Users > User groups > Sections). - Users who don't have the section but do have **Settings** still see uSync in the Settings tree. - To go back to the old layout, set `uSync:Settings:MoveToSection` to `false`. - The uSync API now uses the same check. A user needs the Settings or Synchronisation section to call it. Before, any user with the Content section could call it. (#1156)
### Migrating old editors as you copy a legacy folder
When uSync finds a folder from an earlier version (e.g. `uSync/v18`), the Migrate tab lets you copy it into `uSync/v19`:
![The Migrate tab showing a legacy uSync/v18 folder](https://github.com/KevinJump/uSync/releases/download/v19.0.0-beta01/usync19-migrate-tab.png)
Umbraco 19 replaces some editors, and the copy can now migrate them. The dialog lists the migrations that apply to your files and how many data types each one changes. You choose which ones run:
![The copy dialog listing the Multi Node Tree Picker, single media picker and single dropdown migrations](https://github.com/KevinJump/uSync/releases/download/v19.0.0-beta01/usync19-migrate-modal.png)
- **Multi Node Tree Pickers** move to the Document, Media or Member picker that matches the tree they pick from. Start node, dynamic root, allowed types and min/max items carry over, and stored media values are converted to the media picker format. - **Single media pickers** (a Media Picker that doesn't allow multiple items) move to the new Single Media Picker. - **Single dropdowns** move to the new Single Dropdown.
The migrations rewrite the files as they're copied, so the import that follows is a normal import. The editor changes, so templates and models will see a different model type. Values inside blocks and rich text aren't converted yet. (#1155)
### Importing pre-v19 data type config
Importing data types from older files (without the Migrate tab) now follows Umbraco 19's own migration. The config is updated and, where the config calls for it, the data type moves onto the new editor (e.g. a Media Picker with `multiple: false` becomes a Single Media Picker). The new v19 picker editors also have their own value and dependency mappers.
### Other changes
- Imports run as the user who started them, or the background user. Content is saved and published as the writer in the file, or the importing user, rather than always the super user. - Segment values sync as overrides of their culture. Duplicate block expose entries in old segment-era values are cleaned up on import. - A content schedule's invariant-for-variant flag is now exported and imported. - Library elements used in blocks are tracked as dependencies. - Blueprints are exported again when they or their folder are moved. Importing a blueprint for a content type that can't have blueprints now fails with a clear message. - Publish failure messages name the properties that failed validation. - SignalR and the uSync API accept Umbraco 19's cookie-based backoffice login. - `@jumoo/usync` (the client types other packages build against) is now published to npmjs.org. v19 prereleases use the `next-19` tag. (#1143)
## Breaking
- Members marked obsolete for removal in v18 or v19 have been removed. If your code builds on uSync's services, handlers, mappers or serializers, check the [changelog](https://github.com/KevinJump/uSync/blob/v19/main/CHANGELOG.md) for the full list and their replacements. Members marked for v20 are still there. (#1161)
## Known issues
- uSync still uses `Constants.Security.SuperUserId`, which Umbraco 19 marks obsolete. It works on 19.0.0-beta1 and will be updated in a later release. (#1162)
## What's Changed * Publish @jumoo/usync to npmjs.org with trusted publishing by @KevinJump in https://github.com/KevinJump/uSync/pull/1143 * Merge v17/main into v18/main (2026-10-26) by @KevinJump in https://github.com/KevinJump/uSync/pull/1146 * Show 18.x as the dashboard version fallback on v18 by @henryjump in https://github.com/KevinJump/uSync/pull/1148 * Migrate deprecated editors in the legacy flow by @KevinJump in https://github.com/KevinJump/uSync/pull/1155 * Show uSync in its own section by default by @KevinJump in https://github.com/KevinJump/uSync/pull/1156 * Label PRs with their expected release by @KevinJump in https://github.com/KevinJump/uSync/pull/1158 * Remove members marked obsolete for v18 and v19 by @KevinJump in https://github.com/KevinJump/uSync/pull/1161
**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/KevinJump/uSync/compare/v18.2.0...v19.0.0-beta01

item.title: Publicis Connector 17.0.2
item.description:
### Fixed
- A job submitted in the background could create two Publicis orders. If the scheduled check sent a job while its queued submission was still waiting, the queued submission sent it again, and the job could end up linked to the order Publicis wasn't working on. Each job is now reloaded before it is sent and skipped if it already has an order. A check that times out waiting for another check to finish now stops instead of running anyway, and the job is sent on the next scheduled check.
### Changed
- When a job is sent to Publicis, the connector logs the job and its Publicis order number at Information. - Dependency updates.
**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/Jumoo/TranslatePlus-Connector/compare/v17.0.1...v17.0.2

item.title: uSync Complete 18.3.0
item.description:
Forward-ports v17.6.0 from v17/main.
### Added - Publisher: approvals. A server can require approval for content pushes and pulls; the push or pull stops after the report until someone in the server's approver groups approves or declines it. Turn it on with "Require approval" on the server's Permissions view. Settings pushes and pulls are not affected - Publisher: an approved push or pull is sent again and the target re-checked before anything is applied, showing anything that changed since the request - Publisher: Approvals dashboard in the Content section (requests waiting for you, your requests, history), shown only when approvals are in use - Publisher: approval emails to approvers and requesters when SMTP is configured, overridable with templates in `~/uSync/emails/`, plus `PublisherApprovalRequestedNotification`, `PublisherApprovalDecidedNotification` and `PublisherApprovalFinishedNotification` - Publisher: the Sync Queue. Turn on "Allow queuing" on a server's Permissions view to get an "Add to queue" action and a per-user Sync Queue dashboard in the Content section, for pushing several items, of any type, together - Single-call background API: `POST Publisher/Start` and `POST Exporter/Start`, with `GET Exporter/Download/{id}` for a finished export - Background runs that are queued, scheduled or running can be cancelled from the Background screen
### Changed - Publisher: the push and pull buttons only appear for user groups whose default permissions allow a push or pull - Publisher: a media file is not sent when the target already has an identical copy at the same path; the media item is still synced - Publisher: the first step of a push or pull says it is finding items, and how many it found - Publisher: the push, pull and add to queue actions sit in their own section of the actions menu - The Restore points screen uses a workspace view - Bumped `jumoo.processing` to 18.3.0 - Bumped uSync to 18.2.0
### Fixed - Publisher: the push dialog no longer collapses to nothing in Safari 26.4 - Publisher: progress during a push or pull updates as items are processed - Publisher: import failures are shown in the push and pull result - Publisher: pushing from the content editor no longer goes ahead when the save and publish step is cancelled - Publisher: the current server is recognised when the site is reached over a different scheme, port or letter case than its configured url - Importing user groups exported from Umbraco 13 keeps their permissions - Push and pull no longer fail on some hosts with "The converter for derived type 'System.Collections.IDictionary' does not support metadata writes or reads" - TimeMachine: the timeline refreshes when you come back to it - Exporter: `GetExport` returns Not Found or Bad Request for an unknown or invalid export, rather than a server error - The Background screen shows its process and queue lists again - Publisher: spelling and pluralisation fixes in result messages

item.title: Translation Manager 18.4.0
item.description:
Forward-ported from v17 (17.9.4 and 17.10.0): approval error handling and a save-only auto-approve option (Jumoo/Jumoo.TranslationManager#85), link updater fixes for separate-tree sites, and Jumoo.Processing 18.3.0. On v18 the save/publish checks also cover element items, which are saved through the same content accessor.
- Add: `Translation:ContinueOnApprovalError` (appsettings only, off by default). When it's on, approving a job skips any item that fails to save or publish, records the error in the job history, and carries on with the rest, so only the broken items are left to approve again. Background approval already skipped failed items - Add: when items are skipped this way, the approval results dialog now lists them (across every page of the approval) and counts only the items that were actually approved. Before, it reported every selected item as approved - Change: a save or publish that fails without throwing an exception is now treated as a failed approval. This covers a notification handler cancelling it, the target's parent not being published in that culture, or invalid content. Before, these failures were ignored and the item was marked Approved even though nothing was published. With the setting above off, the approval now stops with the reason, which is also written to the job history. With it on, the item is skipped. A failed publish also rolls back the save, so the item's content is left as it was. **Connectors that call `TranslationJobService.Progress()` directly** (e.g. to auto-approve the items they've just imported) get this too: a failure that used to pass silently now throws, unless the site has `Translation:ContinueOnApprovalError` on - Change: the job-level approved/published notifications (`TranslationJobApprovedNotification` / `TranslationJobPublishedNotification`) and the "Approved"/"Published" job history entries now only happen once every item on the job is approved. Before, they fired for every page of a paged approval, and when only some of a job's items were approved. This applies to connectors calling `Progress()` directly as well. `TranslationJobPartialApprovalNotification` still fires for each batch, now with only the items that were actually approved (and not at all when none were) - Change: an item that approval leaves untouched - a `TranslationNodeApprovingNotification` handler cancelled it, or its source or target content can't be found - is now listed as skipped, with the reason in the job history. Before, it was counted (and reported) as approved - Add: for developers - `TranslationJobService.Progress(job, nodes, TranslationProgressOptions)` returns a `TranslationProgressResult` with the processed and failed items and the resulting job status, and `CheckAndUpdateJobStatusAsync` returns the status it sets. `TranslationProgressOptions.ContinueOnError` defaults to the site's `Translation:ContinueOnApprovalError` setting, which is also what the existing `Progress` overloads use. `ITranslationAprovalService.ApproveWithResultAsync` returns the items that were skipped. The existing `Progress` / `CheckAndUpdateJobStatus` / `ApproveAsync` signatures are unchanged, and `TranslationJobService` has a new constructor taking a `TranslationConfigService` (the old one is obsolete) - Fix: on a site upgraded from an older version, a property could be sent to translation twice, for example as two identical segments in an XLIFF file. This affected items that were already waiting for translation before the upgrade and were then updated. They now correct themselves the next time the item is updated (Jumoo/Jumoo.TranslationManager.Issues#87) - Fix: a block containing a culture-variant nested block list (or a culture-variant rich text editor with blocks), sitting on an invariant block property on a culture-variant page, wasn't fully translated. The items inside the nested list (and the blocks inside the rich text) weren't sent for translation, and the nested items weren't exposed in the target language either, so they showed as drafts there and didn't render (forward-ported from v17, Jumoo/Jumoo.TranslationManager#125) - Add: a "Save only (do not publish)" option under "Automatic approval" in a translation set's processing options. Since background approval was added, auto-approve has always published; with this on, auto-approved translations are saved as drafts instead, so a translator can check them before they go live - Fix: dates in the backoffice (the job view's items table and elsewhere) were shown in UTC rather than the editor's own time zone - an hour behind during BST, for example. The API now returns every date as UTC with its offset, so the browser shows local time - Fix: approving with "Approve in Background" ticked (with `Translation:backgroundApproval` on) left the approval dialog blank, both while the approval ran and after it finished. It now shows the progress and the results. The approval itself always worked - Fix: on a separate-tree set, links in rich text and Multi URL Picker properties on the translated page kept pointing at the master site's pages after approval. They're now updated to the related page on the target site. The picker links had never been updated (a check in the link updater was the wrong way round), and rich text links were missed because Umbraco stores the rich text html escaped inside its json value (Jumoo/Jumoo.TranslationManager.Issues#108) - Change: the link updater logs (at debug) each link it maps, and why it leaves one unchanged, and only logs "Updating property" when a value actually changed - Fix: translating a culture-variant block property no longer leaves the source language's element values (or expose entries) on the target page - Fix: links to content are now updated on the target site when the content's id is upper case or the link is url encoded (`%7BlocalLink:`), or written without a leading slash, matching how Umbraco itself reads them - Fix: links are kept when a translator edits a value in Translation Manager's rich text editor, which now has link and unlink buttons - Fix: on a fresh install where another package publishes content at startup (for example uSync with `ImportAtStartup`), Translation Manager no longer logs `no such table` errors for each item. Its content handlers now wait until its tables exist - Fix: background translation tasks that fail or are cancelled now show the error, instead of "Processing in background" forever - Fix: the "translation jobs created" headline is now localised - Add: a separator sits above Translation Manager's actions in the content actions menu - Build: Jumoo.Processing 18.3.0 (and `@jumoo/processing` ^18.3.0), which carries the background pipeline fixes from Processing 17.5.0. uSync.Complete uses the same library, so a site with uSync.Complete installed may also need its latest v18 release - Build: dependency updates (HtmlAgilityPack 1.13.1 lock files, Microsoft.NET.Test.Sdk 18.11.0)

item.title: uSync Complete 17.6.0
item.description: - New in uSync.Publisher: approvals. A server can require approval for content pushes and pulls to and from it. The push or pull stops after the report until someone in the server's approver groups approves or declines it. Turn it on with "Require approval" on the server's Permissions view, where you also pick the approver groups (admins can always approve) and how many days a request waits before it expires. Settings pushes and pulls are not affected - When a push or pull is approved, uSync sends it again and re-checks the target before applying it, and shows anything that changed since the request was made - New Approvals dashboard in the Content section, with the requests waiting for you, the requests you have made, and their history. It only appears when approvals are in use - Approvers are emailed when a request needs them, and requesters when theirs is decided or fails, when SMTP is configured. Each email can be overridden by putting a template in `~/uSync/emails/`. Sites can also handle the new `PublisherApprovalRequestedNotification`, `PublisherApprovalDecidedNotification` and `PublisherApprovalFinishedNotification` to send them elsewhere - New in uSync.Publisher: the Sync Queue. Turn on "Allow queuing" on a server's Permissions view and items get an "Add to queue" action (also in the content editor's push menu and on the content and media browser dashboards). Each user has their own queue, shown on the new Sync Queue dashboard in the Content section. Pick the items to send, choose whether each one includes its children, and push them together through the usual push dialog. Items leave the queue once their push goes through. The action and dashboard only appear when a server allows queuing - New single-call background API: `POST Publisher/Start` runs a push, pull or settings push/pull, and `POST Exporter/Start` runs an export, in the background. `GET Exporter/Download/{id}` downloads the finished export - The push and pull buttons now only appear for user groups whose default permissions allow a push or pull - uSync.Publisher no longer sends a media file when the target server already has an identical copy at the same path. The media item is still synced. Pushes and pulls between sites that share a media store (for example one Azure Blob container) no longer upload files the other site can already read - Fix: the push dialog no longer collapses to nothing in Safari 26.4, which left the backoffice looking locked - Fix: progress during a push or pull updates as items are processed again, including the "Uploading to server" and "Packing items" messages - The first step of a push or pull now says it is finding items, and how many it found - Fix: import failures are now shown in the push and pull result - Fix: the TimeMachine timeline refreshes when you come back to it - Fix: the content browser card's focus ring no longer covers the Compare button - Fix: Exporter's `GetExport` returns Not Found or Bad Request for an unknown or invalid export, rather than a server error - Fix: pushing from the content editor no longer goes ahead when you cancel the save and publish step, which pushed the previously published version - Fix: Publisher recognises the server it is running on when the site is reached over a different scheme, port or letter case than its configured url, and a server url no longer matches a different host that starts with the same text - Fix: importing user groups exported from Umbraco 13 now maps their permissions to the current permission names, so the groups keep their permissions - Fix: push and pull no longer fail on some hosts with "The converter for derived type 'System.Collections.IDictionary' does not support metadata writes or reads" - Ready for Umbraco 17.8: the Publisher actions sit in their own section of the actions menu, and the Restore points view no longer logs a deprecation warning - Spelling and pluralisation fixes in Publisher result messages - Requires Jumoo.Processing 17.5.0 and uSync 17.5.0

item.title: Jumoo.Processing 18.3.0
item.description:
Includes everything in 17.5.0, merged forward from `v17/main`.
### Added
- **Headless pipeline runs.** `IPipelineRunner` starts a pipeline in one call - created as a background request, options applied, posted to the processing queue - and returns once it is queued. Over the API: `POST StartPipeline` (`202` with the pipeline id and a status URL, `409` with the running pipeline's id when the concurrency key is held), `GET PipelineStatus/{id}` and `POST CancelPipeline/{id}`. Status reports `Queued`/`Running`/`Scheduled`/`Waiting`/`Completed`/ `Failed`/`Cancelled`; `complete` is only true once the run has finished (a `Waiting` run has not), and errors carry the message, action and step but no stack trace. - **Cancel.** A new `Cancelled` pipeline status (added at the end of `PipelineStatus`, so existing values don't move) and a `CancelRequested` flag on the pipeline state. Cancel is cooperative: it takes effect before the next step, and the strategy's clean runs. The `@jumoo/processing` client treats `Cancelled` like `Failed`. `PipelineCleanupJob` removes cancelled pipelines along with completed and failed ones, and never removes waiting ones. - **Concurrency keys.** `IPipelineProcessor.GetConcurrencyKey(strategy, options)` (default `null`). Every way of starting a pipeline gets the processor's key; while one pipeline holding a key is `Running`, `Background` or `Scheduled`, another with the same key is refused, and a `Waiting` one can't resume. Stored in a new indexed `ConcurrencyKey` column on `Jumoo_Pipelines`. An interactive pipeline left `Running` by a closed browser stops holding its key after `Jumoo:Processing:Pipelines:ConcurrencyKeyIdleTimeout` (default one hour). A background one stops holding its key once nothing will run it - no queue row left, or one out of attempts - and it has been quiet for a queue lease. The check and the save take the processing write lock, so two nodes can't both get the same key. - **"Already running" is a 409 everywhere.** `CreatePipeline`, `UpdatePipeline` and `ProcessPipeline` (resume) answer a held concurrency key with `409` and a `PipelineConflictProblemDetails` body - a `ProblemDetails` with the holder's `runningPipelineId` and the `concurrencyKey`, the same fields `StartPipeline`'s `409` carries. Every other failure is still a `400`. In the backoffice, `<jumoo-pipeline>` shows an inline "Already running" state (with the holder's status, when the user can see it) instead of an error toast over an empty modal, and fires `pipeline-conflict`. `getPipelineConflict(error)` reads the body off a failed request. - **Resume.** `IPipelineRunner.ResumeAsync(id, user, expectedAction)` moves a `Waiting` pipeline on, onto the processing queue, so the rest of the run needs no browser - for an action with `WaitOnAction` that waits on something outside the pipeline, such as an approval. Pass the action it should be waiting at, and a second resume is refused with the new `PipelineRunRejectedReason.NotWaiting`, so the run only moves on once. The status check, the concurrency key and the move to the queue are one write. A default interface member, so existing implementers still load. - **Pause, resume and finish notifications.** `PipelineWaitingNotification` when a top-level pipeline stops at an action that waits, `PipelineResumedNotification` (with who resumed it) from `ResumeAsync`, and `PipelineFinishedNotification` when one completes, fails or is cancelled. Each is raised once, by the processing that got the pipeline there. - **`ProcessingConstants` is public**, so packages can write `[ProcessingSwagger(ProcessingConstants.ApiName)]` rather than the literal `"processing"`. - **Run summaries.** `IPipelineProcessor.GetSummary(pipeline)` (default `null`) fills the status's `summary`. Register your own `IPipelineRunSummary` type with `AddPipelineRunSummaryType<T>()`. - **Node affinity.** `IPipelineProcessor.RequiresNodeAffinity` (default `false`) keeps a processor's background work on the node that queued it, for steps that keep working state on local disk. Only that node can claim the pipeline's queue rows; if it stops heartbeating for a queue lease, the pipeline fails with "Processing node lost". A default interface member, so existing processors load unchanged.
### Changed
- **`@jumoo/processing` now publishes to npmjs.org**, not the Azure DevOps npm feed, which stops being anonymously readable in 2027. Pin the major you need (`^18`); nightlies are on the `next-18` dist-tag. Remove any `@jumoo:registry=` line from your `.npmrc`, then regenerate your lock file. - **Pipelines are private to the user who started them.** `PipelineProcessorBase.CanAccessPipeline` now allows the pipeline's creator or a member of the Umbraco admin group, rather than any backoffice user. Pipelines with no recorded owner stay open as before. Processors that override it and call `base` first inherit the change. - Options passed to `CreatePipeline` are applied before the pipeline is first saved, so the concurrency key is checked at create. - A step that posts to the background straight into an action with `WaitOnAction` now leaves the pipeline `Waiting`. It used to stay `Background` with nothing queued to run it. - A pipeline that stops at an action with `WaitOnAction` becomes a background request, wherever it was started: it is waiting on something outside it, not on the browser, so closing the `<jumoo-pipeline>` dialog no longer clears it. Actions with only an `Element` are unchanged. - **A failed step is no longer retried from the queue.** Retrying re-ran the same step and repeated whatever it did before failing, so the queue row is now removed. Infrastructure failures (pipeline not found, an exception outside the step) still retry with backoff. - The queue endpoints (`ListQueue`, `PeekItem`, `ProcessQueue`, `DeleteQueue`) now need the admin group as well as backoffice access. - The queue worker runs as the user who started the pipeline. - `PipelineCleanupJob` runs the strategy's `Clean` before removing a finished pipeline, so working files a strategy keeps on disk no longer outlive it.
### Fixed
- **"SQLite Error 6: database table is locked".** Every queue, status and pipeline-cache write now takes a write lock in `umbracoLock` first, as Umbraco's own services do, so writers queue behind each other instead of deadlocking. - Queue dates are returned as UTC, so a queued item's scheduled time no longer shows an hour out.

item.title: uSync Complete 17.6.0-rc2
item.description:
Release candidate for 17.6.0.
## What's changed
- New in uSync.Publisher: approvals. A server can require approval for content pushes and pulls to and from it. The push or pull stops after the report until someone in the server's approver groups approves or declines it. Turn it on with "Require approval" on the server's Permissions view, where you also pick the approver groups (admins can always approve) and how many days a request waits before it expires. Settings pushes and pulls are not affected - When a push or pull is approved, uSync sends it again and re-checks the target before applying it, and shows anything that changed since the request was made - New Approvals dashboard in the Content section, with the requests waiting for you, the requests you have made, and their history. It only appears when approvals are in use - Approvers are emailed when a request needs them, and requesters when theirs is decided or fails, when SMTP is configured. Each email can be overridden by putting a template in `~/uSync/emails/`. Sites can also handle the new `PublisherApprovalRequestedNotification`, `PublisherApprovalDecidedNotification` and `PublisherApprovalFinishedNotification` to send them elsewhere - New in uSync.Publisher: the Sync Queue. Turn on "Allow queuing" on a server's Permissions view and items get an "Add to queue" action (also in the content editor's push menu and on the content and media browser dashboards). Each user has their own queue, shown on the new Sync Queue dashboard in the Content section. Pick the items to send, choose whether each one includes its children, and push them together through the usual push dialog. Items leave the queue once their push goes through. The action and dashboard only appear when a server allows queuing - New single-call background API: `POST Publisher/Start` runs a push, pull or settings push/pull, and `POST Exporter/Start` runs an export, in the background. `GET Exporter/Download/{id}` downloads the finished export - The push and pull buttons now only appear for user groups whose default permissions allow a push or pull - uSync.Publisher no longer sends a media file when the target server already has an identical copy at the same path. The media item is still synced. Pushes and pulls between sites that share a media store (for example one Azure Blob container) no longer upload files the other site can already read - Fix: the push dialog no longer collapses to nothing in Safari 26.4, which left the backoffice looking locked - Fix: progress during a push or pull updates as items are processed again, including the "Uploading to server" and "Packing items" messages - The first step of a push or pull now says it is finding items, and how many it found - Fix: import failures are now shown in the push and pull result - Fix: the TimeMachine timeline refreshes when you come back to it - Fix: the content browser card's focus ring no longer covers the Compare button - Fix: Exporter's `GetExport` returns Not Found or Bad Request for an unknown or invalid export, rather than a server error - Fix: pushing from the content editor no longer goes ahead when you cancel the save and publish step, which pushed the previously published version - Fix: Publisher recognises the server it is running on when the site is reached over a different scheme, port or letter case than its configured url, and a server url no longer matches a different host that starts with the same text - Fix: importing user groups exported from Umbraco 13 now maps their permissions to the current permission names, so the groups keep their permissions - Fix: push and pull no longer fail on some hosts with "The converter for derived type 'System.Collections.IDictionary' does not support metadata writes or reads" - Ready for Umbraco 17.8: the Publisher actions sit in their own section of the actions menu, and the Restore points view no longer logs a deprecation warning - Spelling and pluralisation fixes in Publisher result messages - Requires Jumoo.Processing 17.5.0 and uSync 17.5.0

item.title: Jumoo.Processing 17.5.0
item.description:
### Added
- **Headless pipeline runs.** `IPipelineRunner` starts a pipeline in one call - created as a background request, options applied, posted to the processing queue - and returns once it is queued. Over the API: `POST StartPipeline` (`202` with the pipeline id and a status URL, `409` with the running pipeline's id when the concurrency key is held), `GET PipelineStatus/{id}` and `POST CancelPipeline/{id}`. Status reports `Queued`/`Running`/`Scheduled`/`Waiting`/`Completed`/ `Failed`/`Cancelled`; `complete` is only true once the run has finished (a `Waiting` run has not), and errors carry the message, action and step but no stack trace. - **Cancel.** A new `Cancelled` pipeline status (added at the end of `PipelineStatus`, so existing values don't move) and a `CancelRequested` flag on the pipeline state. Cancel is cooperative: it takes effect before the next step, and the strategy's clean runs. The `@jumoo/processing` client treats `Cancelled` like `Failed`. `PipelineCleanupJob` removes cancelled pipelines along with completed and failed ones, and never removes waiting ones. - **Concurrency keys.** `IPipelineProcessor.GetConcurrencyKey(strategy, options)` (default `null`). Every way of starting a pipeline gets the processor's key; while one pipeline holding a key is `Running`, `Background` or `Scheduled`, another with the same key is refused, and a `Waiting` one can't resume. Stored in a new indexed `ConcurrencyKey` column on `Jumoo_Pipelines`. An interactive pipeline left `Running` by a closed browser stops holding its key after `Jumoo:Processing:Pipelines:ConcurrencyKeyIdleTimeout` (default one hour). A background one stops holding its key once nothing will run it - no queue row left, or one out of attempts - and it has been quiet for a queue lease. The check and the save take the processing write lock, so two nodes can't both get the same key. - **"Already running" is a 409 everywhere.** `CreatePipeline`, `UpdatePipeline` and `ProcessPipeline` (resume) answer a held concurrency key with `409` and a `PipelineConflictProblemDetails` body - a `ProblemDetails` with the holder's `runningPipelineId` and the `concurrencyKey`, the same fields `StartPipeline`'s `409` carries. Every other failure is still a `400`. In the backoffice, `<jumoo-pipeline>` shows an inline "Already running" state (with the holder's status, when the user can see it) instead of an error toast over an empty modal, and fires `pipeline-conflict`. `getPipelineConflict(error)` reads the body off a failed request. - **Resume.** `IPipelineRunner.ResumeAsync(id, user, expectedAction)` moves a `Waiting` pipeline on, onto the processing queue, so the rest of the run needs no browser - for an action with `WaitOnAction` that waits on something outside the pipeline, such as an approval. Pass the action it should be waiting at, and a second resume is refused with the new `PipelineRunRejectedReason.NotWaiting`, so the run only moves on once. The status check, the concurrency key and the move to the queue are one write. A default interface member, so existing implementers still load. - **Pause, resume and finish notifications.** `PipelineWaitingNotification` when a top-level pipeline stops at an action that waits, `PipelineResumedNotification` (with who resumed it) from `ResumeAsync`, and `PipelineFinishedNotification` when one completes, fails or is cancelled. Each is raised once, by the processing that got the pipeline there. - **`ProcessingConstants` is public**, so packages can write `[ProcessingSwagger(ProcessingConstants.ApiName)]` rather than the literal `"processing"`. - **Run summaries.** `IPipelineProcessor.GetSummary(pipeline)` (default `null`) fills the status's `summary`. Register your own `IPipelineRunSummary` type with `AddPipelineRunSummaryType<T>()`. - **Node affinity.** `IPipelineProcessor.RequiresNodeAffinity` (default `false`) keeps a processor's background work on the node that queued it, for steps that keep working state on local disk. Only that node can claim the pipeline's queue rows; if it stops heartbeating for a queue lease, the pipeline fails with "Processing node lost". A default interface member, so existing processors load unchanged.
### Changed
- **`@jumoo/processing` now publishes to npmjs.org**, not the Azure DevOps npm feed, which stops being anonymously readable in 2027. Pin the major you need (`^17`); nightlies are on the `next-17` dist-tag. Remove any `@jumoo:registry=` line from your `.npmrc`, then regenerate your lock file. - **Pipelines are private to the user who started them.** `PipelineProcessorBase.CanAccessPipeline` now allows the pipeline's creator or a member of the Umbraco admin group, rather than any backoffice user. Pipelines with no recorded owner stay open as before. Processors that override it and call `base` first inherit the change. - Options passed to `CreatePipeline` are applied before the pipeline is first saved, so the concurrency key is checked at create. - A step that posts to the background straight into an action with `WaitOnAction` now leaves the pipeline `Waiting`. It used to stay `Background` with nothing queued to run it. - A pipeline that stops at an action with `WaitOnAction` becomes a background request, wherever it was started: it is waiting on something outside it, not on the browser, so closing the `<jumoo-pipeline>` dialog no longer clears it. Actions with only an `Element` are unchanged. - **A failed step is no longer retried from the queue.** Retrying re-ran the same step and repeated whatever it did before failing, so the queue row is now removed. Infrastructure failures (pipeline not found, an exception outside the step) still retry with backoff. - The queue endpoints (`ListQueue`, `PeekItem`, `ProcessQueue`, `DeleteQueue`) now need the admin group as well as backoffice access. - The queue worker runs as the user who started the pipeline. - `PipelineCleanupJob` runs the strategy's `Clean` before removing a finished pipeline, so working files a strategy keeps on disk no longer outlive it.
### Fixed
- **"SQLite Error 6: database table is locked".** Every queue, status and pipeline-cache write now takes a write lock in `umbracoLock` first, as Umbraco's own services do, so writers queue behind each other instead of deadlocking. - Queue dates are returned as UTC, so a queued item's scheduled time no longer shows an hour out.

item.title: Translation Manager 17.9.4
item.description: - Fix: a block containing a culture-variant nested block list (or a culture-variant rich text editor with blocks), sitting on an invariant block property on a culture-variant page, wasn't fully translated. The items inside the nested list (and the blocks inside the rich text) weren't sent for translation, and on 17.9.x the nested items weren't exposed in the target language either, so they showed as drafts there and didn't render - Add: a "Save only (do not publish)" option under "Automatic approval" in a translation set's processing options. Since background approval was added, auto-approve has always published; with this on, auto-approved translations are saved as drafts instead, so a translator can check them before they go live - Add: `Translation:ContinueOnApprovalError` (appsettings only, off by default). When it's on, approving a job skips any item that fails to save or publish, records the error in the job history, and carries on with the rest, so only the broken items are left to approve again. Background approval already skipped failed items (Jumoo/Jumoo.TranslationManager.Issues#81) - Add: when items are skipped this way, the approval results dialog now lists them (across every page of the approval) and counts only the items that were actually approved. Before, it reported every selected item as approved - Change: a save or publish that fails without throwing an exception is now treated as a failed approval. This covers a notification handler cancelling it, the target's parent not being published in that culture, or invalid content. Before, these failures were ignored and the item was marked Approved even though nothing was published. With the setting above off, the approval now stops with the reason, which is also written to the job history. With it on, the item is skipped. A failed publish also rolls back the save, so the item's content is left as it was. **Connectors that call `TranslationJobService.Progress()` directly** (e.g. to auto-approve the items they've just imported) get this too: a failure that used to pass silently now throws, unless the site has `Translation:ContinueOnApprovalError` on - Change: the job-level approved/published notifications (`TranslationJobApprovedNotification` / `TranslationJobPublishedNotification`) and the "Approved"/"Published" job history entries now only happen once every item on the job is approved. Before, they fired for every page of a paged approval, and when only some of a job's items were approved. This applies to connectors calling `Progress()` directly as well. `TranslationJobPartialApprovalNotification` still fires for each batch, now with only the items that were actually approved (and not at all when none were) - Change: an item that approval leaves untouched - a `TranslationNodeApprovingNotification` handler cancelled it, or its source or target content can't be found - is now listed as skipped, with the reason in the job history. Before, it was counted (and reported) as approved - Add: for developers - `TranslationJobService.Progress(job, nodes, TranslationProgressOptions)` returns a `TranslationProgressResult` with the processed and failed items and the resulting job status, and `CheckAndUpdateJobStatusAsync` returns the status it sets. `TranslationProgressOptions.ContinueOnError` defaults to the site's `Translation:ContinueOnApprovalError` setting, which is also what the existing `Progress` overloads use. `ITranslationAprovalService.ApproveWithResultAsync` returns the items that were skipped. The existing `Progress` / `CheckAndUpdateJobStatus` / `ApproveAsync` signatures are unchanged, and `TranslationJobService` has a new constructor taking a `TranslationConfigService` (the old one is obsolete) - Fix: on a site upgraded from an older version, a property could be sent to translation twice, for example as two identical segments in an XLIFF file. This affected items that were already waiting for translation before the upgrade and were then updated. They now correct themselves the next time the item is updated (Jumoo/Jumoo.TranslationManager.Issues#87) - Fix: dates in the backoffice (the job view's items table and elsewhere) were shown in UTC rather than the editor's own time zone - an hour behind during BST, for example. The API now returns every date as UTC with its offset, so the browser shows local time - Fix: approving with "Approve in Background" ticked (with `Translation:backgroundApproval` on) left the approval dialog blank, both while the approval ran and after it finished. It now shows the progress and the results. The approval itself always worked - Build: Jumoo.Processing updated to 17.4.2 (and the `@jumoo/processing` npm minimum to 17.4.2), with Translation Manager's processing options registered with an explicit type discriminator. uSync.Complete uses the same library, so a site with uSync.Complete installed may also need its latest v17 release - Build: dependency updates (HtmlAgilityPack 1.13.1, prettier, vite, and the test packages)

Release candidate for 17.6.0.
## What's changed
- New in uSync.Publisher: approvals. A server can require approval for content pushes and pulls to and from it. The push or pull stops after the report until someone in the server's approver groups approves or declines it. Turn it on with "Require approval" on the server's Permissions view, where you also pick the approver groups (admins can always approve) and how many days a request waits before it expires. Settings pushes and pulls are not affected - When a push or pull is approved, uSync sends it again and re-checks the target before applying it, and shows anything that changed since the request was made - New Approvals dashboard in the Content section, with the requests waiting for you, the requests you have made, and their history. It only appears when approvals are in use - Approvers are emailed when a request needs them, and requesters when theirs is decided or fails, when SMTP is configured. Each email can be overridden by putting a template in `~/uSync/emails/`. Sites can also handle the new `PublisherApprovalRequestedNotification`, `PublisherApprovalDecidedNotification` and `PublisherApprovalFinishedNotification` to send them elsewhere - New single-call background API: `POST Publisher/Start` runs a push, pull or settings push/pull, and `POST Exporter/Start` runs an export, in the background. `GET Exporter/Download/{id}` downloads the finished export - The push and pull buttons now only appear for user groups whose default permissions allow a push or pull - Fix: the push dialog no longer collapses to nothing in Safari 26.4, which left the backoffice looking locked - Fix: progress during a push or pull updates as items are processed again, including the "Uploading to server" and "Packing items" messages - The first step of a push or pull now says it is finding items, and how many it found - Fix: import failures are now shown in the push and pull result - Fix: the TimeMachine timeline refreshes when you come back to it - Fix: the content browser card's focus ring no longer covers the Compare button - Fix: Exporter's `GetExport` returns Not Found or Bad Request for an unknown or invalid export, rather than a server error - Spelling and pluralisation fixes in Publisher result messages - Requires Jumoo.Processing 17.5.0-rc2

item.title: Jumoo.Processing 17.5.0-rc2
item.description:
### Added
- **Headless pipeline runs.** `IPipelineRunner` starts a pipeline in one call - created as a background request, options applied, posted to the processing queue - and returns once it is queued. Over the API: `POST StartPipeline` (`202` with the pipeline id and a status URL, `409` with the running pipeline's id when the concurrency key is held), `GET PipelineStatus/{id}` and `POST CancelPipeline/{id}`. Status reports `Queued`/`Running`/`Scheduled`/`Waiting`/`Completed`/ `Failed`/`Cancelled`; `complete` is only true once the run has finished (a `Waiting` run has not), and errors carry the message, action and step but no stack trace. - **Cancel.** A new `Cancelled` pipeline status (added at the end of `PipelineStatus`, so existing values don't move) and a `CancelRequested` flag on the pipeline state. Cancel is cooperative: it takes effect before the next step, and the strategy's clean runs. The `@jumoo/processing` client treats `Cancelled` like `Failed`. `PipelineCleanupJob` removes cancelled pipelines along with completed and failed ones, and never removes waiting ones. - **Concurrency keys.** `IPipelineProcessor.GetConcurrencyKey(strategy, options)` (default `null`). Every way of starting a pipeline gets the processor's key; while one pipeline holding a key is `Running`, `Background` or `Scheduled`, another with the same key is refused, and a `Waiting` one can't resume. Stored in a new indexed `ConcurrencyKey` column on `Jumoo_Pipelines`. An interactive pipeline left `Running` by a closed browser stops holding its key after `Jumoo:Processing:Pipelines:ConcurrencyKeyIdleTimeout` (default one hour). A background one stops holding its key once nothing will run it - no queue row left, or one out of attempts - and it has been quiet for a queue lease. The check and the save take the processing write lock, so two nodes can't both get the same key. - **"Already running" is a 409 everywhere.** `CreatePipeline`, `UpdatePipeline` and `ProcessPipeline` (resume) answer a held concurrency key with `409` and a `PipelineConflictProblemDetails` body - a `ProblemDetails` with the holder's `runningPipelineId` and the `concurrencyKey`, the same fields `StartPipeline`'s `409` carries. Every other failure is still a `400`. In the backoffice, `<jumoo-pipeline>` shows an inline "Already running" state (with the holder's status, when the user can see it) instead of an error toast over an empty modal, and fires `pipeline-conflict`. `getPipelineConflict(error)` reads the body off a failed request. - **Resume.** `IPipelineRunner.ResumeAsync(id, user, expectedAction)` moves a `Waiting` pipeline on, onto the processing queue, so the rest of the run needs no browser - for an action with `WaitOnAction` that waits on something outside the pipeline, such as an approval. Pass the action it should be waiting at, and a second resume is refused with the new `PipelineRunRejectedReason.NotWaiting`, so the run only moves on once. The status check, the concurrency key and the move to the queue are one write. A default interface member, so existing implementers still load. - **Pause, resume and finish notifications.** `PipelineWaitingNotification` when a top-level pipeline stops at an action that waits, `PipelineResumedNotification` (with who resumed it) from `ResumeAsync`, and `PipelineFinishedNotification` when one completes, fails or is cancelled. Each is raised once, by the processing that got the pipeline there. - **`ProcessingConstants` is public**, so packages can write `[ProcessingSwagger(ProcessingConstants.ApiName)]` rather than the literal `"processing"`. - **Run summaries.** `IPipelineProcessor.GetSummary(pipeline)` (default `null`) fills the status's `summary`. Register your own `IPipelineRunSummary` type with `AddPipelineRunSummaryType<T>()`.
### Changed
- **`@jumoo/processing` now publishes to npmjs.org**, not the Azure DevOps npm feed, which stops being anonymously readable in 2027. Pin the major you need (`^17`); nightlies are on the `next-17` dist-tag. Remove any `@jumoo:registry=` line from your `.npmrc`, then regenerate your lock file. - **Pipelines are private to the user who started them.** `PipelineProcessorBase.CanAccessPipeline` now allows the pipeline's creator or a member of the Umbraco admin group, rather than any backoffice user. Pipelines with no recorded owner stay open as before. Processors that override it and call `base` first inherit the change. - Options passed to `CreatePipeline` are applied before the pipeline is first saved, so the concurrency key is checked at create. - A step that posts to the background straight into an action with `WaitOnAction` now leaves the pipeline `Waiting`. It used to stay `Background` with nothing queued to run it. - A pipeline that stops at an action with `WaitOnAction` becomes a background request, wherever it was started: it is waiting on something outside it, not on the browser, so closing the `<jumoo-pipeline>` dialog no longer clears it. Actions with only an `Element` are unchanged.
